settings.text: The bike was the first thing I ever made with my own hands. When my daughter rode it on family visit day, I felt like a dad again.
Pandas eat it. Schoolchildren used to be caned with it. But now prisoners at Lowdham Grange have found a surprising new use for bamboo — making bicycles out of it.
Bamboo bikes have that cool factor that excites them. There's maths and English in the programme — but it's built into design, creativity and bike mechanics.

settings.stories_lede: The same craft shows up everywhere — on epic journeys, in boardrooms, in classrooms and across the world.
settings.story_title: we build real workshops inside prisons.
settings.story_body_1: Inside HMP Lowdham Grange — a Category-B men's prison in Nottinghamshire — we've built a 2,000 sq ft workshop where Makers take a six-week, OCN-accredited course: from workshop safety and material science through frame construction, mechanics and finishing.
settings.story_body_2: Trusted Makers train as peer instructors — and in the final week, frames are taken apart so the materials serve the next cohort, which is what keeps it affordable.
settings.b2b_image_alt: The Build to Bond workshop inside HMP Lowdham Grange
settings.b2b_title: the bikes Makers build go home to their kids.
settings.b2b_body_1: The most engaged participants progress to Build to Bond — building a children's bamboo balance bike to gift to their own son, daughter, niece or nephew. That bike they keep. The bike goes home; the father stays inside.
settings.b2b_body_2: It's built on the strongest predictor of reduced reoffending there is: keeping family ties alive while a parent is inside. The bike goes home; the bond holds.
settings.b2b_quote: Watching the pride on a father's face when he presents a bike to his child is something special.
